title: Transition Morphology — Door, Way, Breach, Barrier, Perimeter & Recursive Threshold
purpose: Unify the project's growing threshold vocabulary by asking what operation each structure performs on reachable states. Door, Gate, Way, Breach, Veil, Wall, Perimeter, Circuit and nested Box are related but not synonymous.

formal_object.boundary: B separates regions or constrains transitions
formal_object.transition_operator: D(a,x,B,c) -> set of states reachable from x under context c
formal_object.route_cost: w(e) records effort/risk/time/constraint; path preparation can change w without creating a new destination
formal_object.important_boundary: Mathematical graph/topology language is a formal analogy for project organization unless independently tied to a physical model.

access is mediated through an embodied/relational route rather than merely a geometric opening

cut/barrier removed; previously separated reachable sets reconnect

transition_types.graph_effect: edge/path cost decreases; failure probability decreases

project_neighbors: Revelation 22 invitation to water of life

questions: Does a transition edge already exist?
Is the edge open, closed, filtered or hidden?
Is the boundary legitimate/protective, harmful/confining or context-dependent?
Does recurrence change state continuously, discretely at completion, or not at all?
Is access merely possible or actively invited?
Does traversal reveal a nested state-space?
function_matrix.rule: Never classify a Door/Wall/Stone/Mountain as good or bad from object identity alone; classify the operation it performs in context.

derived_mathematical_analogies.analogue: door opens/closes an existing graph edge
breach creates a connection that was absent
road repair/removing stones lowers traversal cost
ritual circuit unlocks state only after completion condition
protective boundary blocks harmful edges while preserving life-giving movement

cross_domain_uses: Biblical reader: distinguish textual threshold functions instead of keyword matching.
Psychology-as-metaphor: distinguish avoidance loops, boundaries, repair routes and state transitions without diagnosing people.
Software/system design: model permissions, APIs, interfaces, firewalls, queues and state machines as typed transitions rather than mystical equivalents.
Economics/institutions: distinguish barriers to entry, gateways, standards, bridges and infrastructure costs.
North/relational atlas: track whether a relationship creates capability, blocks risk, lowers transaction cost or requires a mediator.
Science formalization: only promote analogies to empirical models when variables/measurements are explicitly defined and testable.
